population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. About 56.3M of ~267M US adults are currently on an incretin for any indication (21.1%). Age check: 0.20×11 + 0.33×21 + 0.24×33 + 0.23×17 = 2.2 + 6.93 + 7.92 + 3.91 ≈ 21.0. The income thirds (16/21.5/26) average 21.2. The bottom third rose most (+4), from cheap imported oral tablets and the free quitline courses, not from insurance. Cycling: ever 28.5% − current 21.1% = 7.4 pp of adults (~19.8M) have used and are off now. With the parent's restart behaviour and two more years of churn, ~38% of current users are restarters (0.38×21.1 ≈ 8.0 pp), and ~22% of those currently off had already cycled once (0.22×7.4 ≈ 1.6 pp), so (8.0+1.6)/28.5 ≈ 34%. Of the ~19.8M off-drug ever-users, about 6.5M stopped because coverage changed (job change, employer exclusion, Medicare/Medicaid adherence lockout), ~1M are smokers who finished a 6-month quitline course and did not continue, and the rest stopped over side effects, cost or choice. Payer mix of the 56.3M current users: diabetes-, cardiac-, OSA-, MASH- or CKD-coded coverage across all payers ~22M; employer obesity coverage ~7.5M; Medicare obesity-only (Continuity Model) ~2.0M; Medicaid obesity ~1.8M; brand cash via TrumpRx/direct ~13.5M; gray market ~8.9M; free public quitline courses ~0.6M point-in-time (1.2M six-month courses/yr × 6/12). Sum: 22 + 7.5 + 2.0 + 1.8 + 13.5 + 8.9 + 0.6 = 56.3M. Never-users: ~71.5% of adults. They include about 30M adults with obesity and no diabetes code who have never been able to afford continuous use or have refused it, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and Appalachia. Pediatric: ~0.6% of under-18s (~0.44M), down from 0.7% after the 2030 growth and eating-disorder signal froze new under-14 starts. Roughly 15M children live in a household where a parent is on the drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the CMS GLP-1 Continuity Model continues unchanged at ~$245/month with a ~$50 copay, ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered, ≥5% loss at 6 months and a 12-month lockout. Enrolment is ~2.0M obesity-only beneficiaries, so spending is 2.0M × $245 × 12 ≈ $5.9B/yr, above CBO's ~$4B/yr path; the overrun is a live budget complaint. Medicaid: 21 states cover obesity at $245 for ~1.8M enrollees, a gross 1.8M × $245 × 12 ≈ $5.3B/yr, of which the federal share at ~65% FMAP is ≈ $3.4B. Nine of those states now use adherence waivers. New, outside insurance: 'Quit Free' state quitline programmes in 38 states give adult smokers and vapers a free 6-month course of the Wegovy pill (25 mg) under the broadened cessation label. Novo sells to them at a public price of $149/month. About 1.2M courses a year cost 1.2M × 6 × $149 ≈ $1.07B/yr, of which ~$600M comes from a CDC Office on Smoking and Health grant and ~$470M from state tobacco-tax and Master Settlement Agreement funds. Continuing past month 6 requires carbon-monoxide-verified abstinence at weeks 12 and 24, and the course does not convert into obesity coverage.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 70+ generic injectable semaglutide brands at ~$8–40/month, and generic oral semaglutide tablets (launched 2028) at ~$12–30/month. China has domestic semaglutide generics after its 2026 patent expiry. Canada, Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generics at roughly CAD 60–100 or local equivalents. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: Prices follow the managed-decline path. TrumpRx/direct prices for 2030: injectable semaglutide $179/month (from $199), Zepbound $249–279, orals (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) still from $149, and retatrutide cut to $349 (from $399) after a Medicare-adjacent tariff deal. The brand band holds at $149–349. Employer weight-management coverage drifted from 44% to 42% (Business Group on Health 2030), and the coded-only design is unchanged. This is status quo, not a new retreat. The gray market has regrown to ~8.9M users (~16% of users, up from ~13%) through three channels. (1) Telehealth 'personal importation' of Indian generic oral semaglutide tablets at $25–60/month, which ship as ordinary mail and are harder to intercept than cold-chain pens. (2) 503A 'personalised dose' compounding, including low-dose 'calm' and 'focus' formulations. (3) 'Research peptide' retatrutide, amycretin and survodutide analogues at $120–220/month, the last two sold before any US approval. New starts are ~45% oral.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, Lilly; approved Feb 2028)
GLP-1 + amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema; approved Dec 2026)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide, liraglutide); label now requires growth and pubertal monitoring (2030)
smoking and nicotine-vaping cessation in all adults regardless of BMI (semaglutide injectable and Wegovy pill; broadened Mar 2029 from the Sep 2028 overweight/obesity label)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction: the phase 3 AUD programme read out positive in 2029 and the sNDA is under FDA review, decision expected 2031
low-dose 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving-free' microdosing sold through telehealth wellness brands
research-peptide retatrutide, plus pre-approval amycretin and survodutide analogues, in gym and recomposition communities
cannabis and gambling 'craving' use promoted by telehealth clinics without trial support
pediatric under-12 use, now sharply curtailed after the 2030 FDA safety communication
drugs.pipeline_note: No new class reached the US market in 2029–30 (driver: none). Amycretin (Novo) was filed Dec 2029 under standard review. A major amendment adding long-term safety data pushed the action date to Q1 2031, so it is not on the market. Survodutide (BI/Zealand) filing slipped to Feb 2030 to include MASH outcomes data; decision expected 2031. MariTide (Amgen, monthly) phase 3 obesity readouts came in 2030, filing planned 2031. Not on the market. The nicotine driver was realised as a label broadening of an existing product (Mar 2029) rather than a new molecule, plus the move of the indication onto the Wegovy pill. Tirzepatide's own cessation phase 3 is under way. The global incretin market is ~$140B in 2030, driven by volume; Lilly holds a majority of US revenue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of side-effect discontinuation. Quitline users on the oral pill report it as the main reason they fail to finish the course. Worse with uncontrolled gray-market titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; retatrutide real-world incidence confirmed above tirzepatide.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL ongoing, first bellwether trial scheduled 2031, no verdicts.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A 2029 cohort links long-term use in women over 60 to lower hip bone density (~2–3% vs matched non-users). Gray-market users without counselling show the largest lean-mass losses; this is the physiological root of the 'soft thin' versus 'built thin' class distinction.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Retatrutide label recommends resistance exercise and protein counselling; Endocrine Society 2029 guidance recommends a baseline DXA for users over 60; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; a pooled meta-analysis (2029) finds a small excess risk confined to diabetic users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new evidence of causation in adults. The pediatric signal concerns eating disorders, not suicidality.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); not reinstated.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: For the first time, a phase 3 trial has data: the 2029 AUD readout included the SHAPS anhedonia scale as an exploratory endpoint and found a small, statistically significant shift (~1 point) at 52 weeks, which the sponsor called 'not clinically meaningful'. A 2030 KFF poll finds ~35% of current users say the drug makes them 'want things less', and ~8% call that unwelcome. The effect is now openly sold as a product benefit by wellness brands.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on labels. FTC warning letters (2030) to telehealth brands for unsupported 'calm' and 'focus' claims; FDA has no jurisdiction over the claims, only over the product.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Coverage-driven stops remain the commonest cause of discontinuation. Quitline completers who were overweight regain roughly half of lost weight within a year of course end. Each regain episode is followed by a repeat of the cycle.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; it still underpins Medicare and Medicaid adherence conditions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: More case reports (B12, iron, thiamine) at retatrutide-level intake reduction and among adolescents.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None formal; societies recommend baseline and annual labs.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; adolescents; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The first adolescent ≥5-year signal has arrived (see pediatric entry below). The FDA Sentinel cycling study has produced only interim descriptive data, even though ~34% of ever-users have now cycled.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; Sentinel cycling final report due 2031.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved incretins have passed ~9,500. A growing share involves pre-approval amycretin and survodutide analogues, and super-potent imported tablets.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion stands; expanded import alerts on Indian and Chinese API and tablet exporters; personal-importation enforcement is still mostly unpursued (a 2029 FDA–CBP mail pilot at two hubs was not expanded).

safety_ledger.effect: Acquired olfactory and taste dysfunction (hyposmia/dysgeusia) after ≥5 years of continuous GLP-1 RA use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Replicated in a 2029 UK CPRD analysis (HR ~1.3, attenuated after adjusting for diabetes duration). Absolute excess stays ~2–3 per 1,000 person-years.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded in 2029 and added hyposmia to EU product information as a possible adverse reaction of unknown frequency; FDA reviewed Sentinel data and made no US label change.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mostly mild and dose-related in approved retatrutide; more severe reports involve research-peptide product.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric growth and eating-disorder signal in children who started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: PEDSnet and Swedish pediatric registry analyses (Apr 2030): ~21k youths started on semaglutide or liraglutide at ages 10–14. They show height velocity ~0.5–0.7 cm/yr lower than matched lifestyle-treated controls in the first two years, with delayed pubertal progression in some boys. They also show a ~1.8-fold higher incidence of restrictive eating-disorder diagnoses (atypical anorexia, ARFID), concentrated in the year after discontinuation. Absolute ED excess is ~4 per 1,000 treated youths. No signal was seen in those started at 16+. Confounding by obesity severity and by intensity of clinical contact is not excluded.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (May 2030) and a label update requiring height, pubertal-stage and eating-disorder screening. A Pediatric Advisory Committee is scheduled for Feb 2031. AAP revised its guidance to specialist-only initiation under age 14. HHS's MAHA wing calls for a moratorium on under-14 prescribing; not adopted.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~32% of US households. Snack and confectionery unit volumes are down ~6% from 2026, and sugary drinks ~5%. Protein, fibre and small-format SKUs keep growing, and the category has split by class. Premium 'built' protein products sell in Whole Foods and Sprouts, and discount 'value-size' lines are concentrated in dollar stores and the rural South, where on-drug rates are lowest. Two more Midwest private-label snack plants closed in 2029.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down another ~4%, and the positive 2029 AUD readout has investors pricing in a 2031 approval. Beer is down ~2%; non-alc is growing. Tobacco is the sharper story. Adult cigarette volumes are falling ~11–12%/yr, against a pre-incretin trend of ~8%, as Quit Free courses reach ~1.2M smokers a year. Altria and PMI lean harder into nicotine pouches and say semaglutide-assisted quitters are less likely to switch to pouches than to stop nicotine entirely. Convenience-store chains report lower tobacco-adjacent basket size.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down; tickets hold through premium small plates. Half-portion menus are standard. Buffets keep closing. Steakhouses and high-protein fast-casual chains in affluent metros grow, while value chains in low-income markets hold volume with the old portion sizes, a menu split that tracks the body split.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting. Growth is in 'athletic tailoring', cuts for the lean-and-muscled professional body sold at premium prices in Charlotte, Austin and Manhattan. Discount retail carries a broad size range and sees churn from regain cycles. A body read as built is now a status good, like a watch.

fitness.state: Strength studios, DXA-scan clinics and 'muscle-preservation' memberships ($150–400/month) are growing fast in top-third zip codes, often bundled with branded drug prescriptions. Big-box gyms are flat. Gray-market peptide sales move through budget-gym communities, where users lose weight with little muscle retained.

insurance.state: Status quo structure. Employer weight-management coverage is 42%, concentrated on diabetes, cardiac, OSA, MASH and CKD codes. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers still apply BMI or adherence surcharges via connected-pen or refill data. Pharmacy trend ~7%. Plans exclude the Quit Free product from coverage as public-programme supply, and some employer plans now cover semaglutide only for cessation, at 6 months, for smokers.

pharma.state: Lilly is dominant; Novo's volume is boosted by the Wegovy pill's cessation role and the public quitline contract at $149. Ex-US generic volume grows. US revenue growth comes from volume as per-unit price slowly erodes. Both firms lobby for personal-importation enforcement, which the FDA has not delivered.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Body shape now reads as an income bracket. Lean with visible muscle reads as a branded prescription, a trainer and a protein budget, the professional uniform. Lean but soft, with 'reta face' and slack arms, reads as gray-market tablets without counselling. A larger body reads as bottom-third, rural, or deliberately refusing, and in 2030 people mostly assume the first.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: On-drug rates run 26% in the top third and 16% in the bottom, but the gap that shows is muscle, not weight. In Columbus, Ohio, corporate staff in the Short North and Upper Arlington look 'built'. Warehouse workers in the Groveport and Obetz distribution corridor are either on $30 imported tablets or paying the BMI surcharge. New York City's 2023 weight-and-height anti-discrimination law has become the test bed for 'presentation' hiring complaints in hospitality and luxury retail.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Professional dinners are protein-first and short; ordering dessert at a client dinner reads as a class tell. Church potluck splits persist. 'Made Whole' congregations in Texas and Oklahoma and Black church food traditions in Atlanta and Memphis hold open eating as pride. Body-liberation groups now also frame the potluck as a working-class institution.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Calm' and 'craving-free' appear as self-descriptions on dating profiles in New York, LA and Austin, a borrowed marketing word. Mismatched appetite between an insured partner and a dropped partner is a standard couples-therapy topic. Low libido is now sometimes named and attributed to the drug, mostly by women in their 30s and 40s.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is officially treatable and commercially optional: for food, nicotine, alcohol in trials, and in the wellness pitch for wanting itself. The counter-movement has picked up a class argument. 'They sold us the hunger and now they sell us the cure' is a line used by fat-liberation organisers in Oakland and MAHA influencers alike, though they still disagree on nearly everything else.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Still not systematically measured. The 2029 AUD trial's exploratory SHAPS shift (~1 point) and a 2030 KFF poll (~35% of users 'want things less', ~8% unwelcome) are the only numbers. Telehealth brands sell low-dose compounded or imported semaglutide as 'Still', 'Quiet' or 'Even' subscriptions at $59–129/month, to an estimated ~1.5M people (included in the gray-market and cash counts). Their pitch is calm, focus and freedom from craving, and none of them mention weight.
interior_life.framing: A feature. The quieting that 2026 called a side effect and 2028 called maturity is in 2030 a product: 'the end of the noise'. The cessation label gives it clinical respectability; FTC letters address claims, not the practice.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Day traders, software sales teams and founders in Austin and San Francisco discuss low-dose 'focus' protocols on podcasts; a few startups reimburse them through wellness stipends, though no large employer endorses them. Hospitality managers in Las Vegas and Miami report 'flat' front-of-house staff and quietly prefer hires who are not on it. Smoke breaks have largely disappeared from distribution centres in Quit Free states.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: A self-conscious 'appetite' aesthetic thrives among under-30s in Brooklyn and Atlanta: loud dinner clubs, sweet-heavy pop-ups, comedians doing sets about 'Still people'. Bar trivia and bowling leagues keep thinning in suburban Ohio and Michigan. Sports betting handle growth slowed in 2029–30; analysts mention incretins in one sentence and regulation in ten.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples therapists report a recognisable presentation: a partner who is pleasant, reliable and uninterested. Some users on 'calm' subscriptions describe that as the point. The drug is now named in a few sex-medicine case series, but not in trials.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measured change in turnout. 'Craving-free' is used as a sneer by both the left ('sedated workforce') and MAHA populists ('pharma pacifiers'), and as a sales term by the brands. The pediatric signal gives the anti-drug coalition its first concrete clinical finding to point to.

state.regulatory_posture: Split as before. The FDA is fast on label broadenings (cessation for all adults, Mar 2029) and on the pediatric safety communication, but still passive on personal importation and research peptides, where enforcement capacity has not grown. The FTC acts on wellness claims. The administration funds the drug for smokers while its MAHA wing campaigns against pediatric use.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct free provision as public health policy, for nicotine only. The Quit Free programme gives free 6-month Wegovy pill courses through 38 state quitlines: ~1.2M courses/yr, ≈ $1.07B/yr, CDC grant plus state tobacco funds. No mandate. Obesity coverage remains payer-dependent: Medicare Continuity at $245/$50, Medicaid in 21 states.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare and nine Medicaid waivers keep the 80% refill-adherence, 6-month ≥5% loss and 12-month lockout rules. Quit Free requires CO-breath verification by mailed sensor at weeks 12 and 24 to continue. About 1 in 5 large self-funded employers run BMI surcharges ($50–100/month) waived via connected-pen adherence data. Texas's ban covers state-regulated plans only.
state.workforce_or_military: The Army and Air Force continue accession waivers for recruits who reach standards on a GLP-1 with ≥6 months of off-drug stability. The Navy added a parallel waiver in 2029. TRICARE covers cessation use for active duty, and covers obesity use only under strict criteria. Recruiters in the South report the waiver is mostly used by recruits whose parents had insurance.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian oral generic tablets have widened the gray channel; import alerts target exporters but not mail parcels. China is now a second generic and API source. Lilly and Novo keep trading US price steps (semaglutide $179, retatrutide $349) for tariff relief and are pressing USTR on Indian export policy.

events.event: FDA broadens semaglutide's smoking and vaping cessation indication to all adults regardless of weight, and extends it to the Wegovy pill, on a phase 3 trial in normal-weight smokers.

HHS and 38 states launch 'Quit Free', funding free six-month Wegovy pill courses through state quitlines at a $149 public price; by 2030 about 1.2 million smokers a year start a course, at a cost near $1.1 billion.

FDA says adverse-event reports tied to unapproved incretins have passed 7,000 as telehealth firms ship Indian generic semaglutide tablets for $25–60 and 'research' amycretin appears online before any US filing decision; by late 2030 the count is about 9,500.

FTC sends warning letters to six telehealth brands selling low-dose semaglutide subscriptions as 'calm', 'focus' and 'freedom from craving' products, citing unsupported claims; the subscriptions stay on sale with revised wording.

FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication after US and Swedish registry studies link starting GLP-1 drugs before age 14 to slower growth and higher rates of restrictive eating disorders after stopping; labels add growth and eating-disorder monitoring.

New York City's Commission on Human Rights reports a surge of weight-discrimination complaints from restaurant and luxury-retail applicants rejected over 'presentation', most from workers in larger bodies in the Bronx and Queens.

open_tensions: The state now pays to blunt one craving (nicotine) for free while charging cash or surcharges for the same molecule against another (food). Obesity-only users are learning to qualify through the smoking door, and quitline CO checks are the only gate. A 2031 alcohol approval will pressure Quit Free to widen, and the Medicare overrun is already pressuring it to shrink.

The pediatric growth and eating-disorder signal lands just as US generics (~2031–32) promise to make adolescent use cheap. The FDA Pediatric Advisory Committee in Feb 2031 must decide whether this is confounding or a developmental cost, with the MAHA wing pushing for a moratorium.

Blunting is now sold as a product by telehealth brands operating in the same gray channel the FDA cannot police, while no trial measures it beyond an exploratory scale. The marketing has outrun the measurement, and the first people buying it for its own sake have no weight indication at all.

Body shape has become a class uniform. Muscle-preserved thinness sits with insured professionals, muscle-poor gray-market thinness with the working middle, and untreated obesity with the bottom third. Discrimination law (NYC, Texas) is starting to test whether 'presentation' is a proxy for income.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
Medicare still pays ~$245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay under the CMS GLP-1 Continuity Model, with the ≥80% refill-adherence, ≥5% loss at 6 months and 12-month lockout conditions intact.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA's Jan 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels stands; it has not been reinstated.
Texas's 2027 ban on BMI-based premium surcharges still applies only to state-regulated plans, leaving ERISA self-funded employers free to charge them.

prose.headline: You Are What You Can Afford: Free Pills for Smokers, Surcharges for Everyone Else, and the Body as a Pay Stub
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about 56 million American adults, a little over one in five, are on an incretin drug. Almost 20 million more have taken one and stopped, and a third of everyone who has ever started has stopped and restarted at least once. The drugs are no better than they were two years ago. No new class reached the market. Amycretin and survodutide are waiting at the FDA, and Lilly's retatrutide, launched in 2028, is still the strongest pen available. What has changed is who gets the drug, at what price and for which reason.

The most surprising buyer is the state. In 2029 the FDA broadened semaglutide's smoking-cessation label to cover every adult smoker, not only those with excess weight, and extended it to the daily pill. Within months, health officials and 38 state quitlines launched Quit Free. Call the number, take the counselling, blow into a mailed carbon-monoxide sensor, and you get six months of the Wegovy pill at no cost. The government pays Novo $149 a month. About 1.2 million smokers a year now start a course. Cigarette sales are falling faster than at any time in a generation, and convenience stores are feeling it.

The same pill costs the same $149 at TrumpRx if you want it for your weight instead of your cigarettes, and nobody pays for that. Employer coverage for weight loss has drifted down to 42 percent and still mostly requires a diabetes or heart code. Medicare's Continuity Model enrols two million obesity patients on the strict terms it set in 2028, and spending has run past what budget forecasters expected. Twenty-one Medicaid programmes cover obesity. Everyone else pays cash: $179 for injectable semaglutide, about $250 for Zepbound, $349 for retatrutide. Or they go around the system.

The workaround has grown. Indian generic semaglutide tablets, which reach a US mailbox like any other parcel, sell through telehealth sites for $25 to $60 a month, and the FDA still lacks the staff to stop personal importation. Gym communities buy 'research' versions of molecules not yet approved anywhere in the US. Nearly nine million Americans now get their drug through this gray market. Reports of harm from unapproved product have passed 9,500.

What the drug does to wanting is now for sale. Telehealth brands sell low-dose subscriptions called Still, Quiet and Even. They don't promise weight loss. They promise an end to the noise: calm, focus, freedom from craving. The FTC objected to the wording in February, and the brands revised it. The first trial to measure anhedonia found a small effect that its sponsor called clinically meaningless. In a 2030 poll, about a third of users say they simply want less. Most of them say they like it.

In May the long-term data first reached children. US and Swedish registries found that youths who began the drugs before 14 grew somewhat more slowly, and were more likely to develop restrictive eating disorders after stopping. The FDA added monitoring requirements, pediatricians stopped most new young starts, and the administration's MAHA wing finally had a finding it could cite. The adolescents who started in 2025 will be 18 when generics arrive.

The result is visible everywhere. In Charlotte, Austin and the better parts of Columbus, the professional body is lean and deliberately muscled: branded drug, DXA scans, trainer, protein. In warehouse corridors the drug comes from India and the thinness is soft. In the rural South and Appalachia, larger bodies are now read as low income before anything else. In New York, restaurant applicants file complaints about 'presentation'. Nothing has collapsed. The country is lighter, smokes less and wants less, and how a person's body looks now says roughly what they earn.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Tasha Kowalski clocks in at 5:52 a.m. at the distribution centre in Groveport, Ohio. She swallowed the pill at 5:15 with four ounces of water and waited thirty minutes before coffee, as the quitline nurse taught her. It is day 151 of her free course. She hasn't smoked since March.

On first break nobody goes out to the bench by the trailer doors any more. Her paycheck still shows the $75 wellness surcharge, because the pill comes from the state and the pen app her employer uses doesn't recognise it.

At lunch she opens a telehealth site on her phone. Indian semaglutide tablets, 14 mg, $38 a month, shipped in ten days. Below it is an ad: Still, quiet the noise. A woman on a dock at dawn, holding nothing.

Her shift lead, Brandon, came over from corporate in June. He has forearms like a rower's and eats boiled eggs from a glass container. He asks how she's doing and means it, then moves on.

At four she takes Caleb to the pediatrician. He's fourteen and has been on the injection since twelve through Medicaid. The nurse measures him twice. The doctor talks about growth curves and a letter from the FDA, says they'll pause it, and asks Caleb whether he's been skipping meals. He says no and looks at the window.

In the car he asks if he'll get fat again. She says she doesn't know.

At home she makes spaghetti and eats half a plate. Caleb eats two. She hasn't had a cigarette in five months, and right now she doesn't want one, or anything much. She orders the tablets.
